cards.ciVerifiedNote: Stays false, and the reason changed. The old reason -- no workflow runs tools/collect_s12_acceptance_evidence.py -- stopped being true when .github/workflows/s12-acceptance-evidence.yml landed with #283: CI derives the bundle, holds it to its shape and to the head it was derived at, and uploads it, and run 36851875128 did exactly that at 40b3ec78 (an ancestor of this tree). The new reason is that none of it is attested: the receipt below is built offline from gh api JSON and its receiptSha256 is a hash rather than a signature, so a run id forged in the receipt and the registry together survives re-hashing (#295 r2 F1, reproduced). ciVerifiedRun and the receipt are therefore a MEASUREMENT RECORD, not the basis of a true claim -- the checker binds them to each other, holds the receipt to an exact key set, and refuses impliesCiVerified: true outright until a receipt carries something it did not write. A CI-produced attested receipt is the follow-up card. The restore drill remains ci-verified by core.yml owned CX01 steps at this tree.

requiredSteps: Hold the bundle to its shape and to this head
Record that the two named observations were derived here
ciVerifiedRun.why: The dispatch at #283's final head, which is an ancestor of this registry's verifiedAgainst.tree. The gate step is what makes it evidence rather than a green tick: check_s12_acceptance_shape.py re-derives the verdict and the seventeen item sources from the collector and refuses a bundle whose codeSha is not the head the run checked out, so a fabricated PASS cannot pass it. Every field here is bound to the receipt, which was built by tools/record_vf_cl_ci_receipt.py from three gh api documents and carries their digests -- the first version of this block was prose a checker read for shape, and five fabrications passed it.

notApplicable: ciVerified: a review card ships documents, not code CI executes

independentlyReviewed: this card IS the review function, so an independent review of it is the reviewer's act and not the owner's. Card 285 left the field false deliberately: the owner may not raise it, and Codex raising it is the only way it becomes true. Card 284 closed the other four cards' review blockers and did not reach this one, so it is now the only card without an independent review.

verifiedAgainst.candidateNote: coord/train63a-ci-0847 is the train 63 landing CANDIDATE, not integration. Every claim re-derived here is about that candidate tree. When it reaches integration/all-agents-unified the claims must be re-verified and re-recorded at the landed SHA -- rule 8 reports until they are, because an ancestry relation is not a licence to carry a candidate's evidence forward.
verifiedAgainst.note: Card 285 re-recorded this block at the train 63 candidate (train 62 plus the single merge of #381). The previous entry named the train 11 candidate 25f43a25, which is an ancestor of this tree and still passed rule 8 only because it had never reached integration -- a claim that is technically admissible and 52 trains stale. All 56 manifest checks were re-applied here independently of the checker and all 56 hold, which is what re-derives implemented. locallyVerified was re-measured per card at this tree (see reverification). ciVerified is unchanged: the manifest still asserts nothing for VF-CL-01/02/03/05 and the hosted lane cannot attribute a directory run to one card, so the per-card attribution below records what the run does and does not show rather than upgrading the claim.

Attempt 1 of this run id concluded failure on one unrelated real-PG setup error (test_kernel_cancel_bridge_real_pg, NODE-0030 uncertain delivery; 8,623 passed, 0 failures, 1 error) and the failed job was re-run. The three owned CX01 steps succeeded in attempt 1 as well, so the drill measurement did not depend on the re-run; the attempt is recorded because a reader checking this run id sees both.

reverification.environment: Python 3.14.7, docker hidden from PATH, real PostgreSQL only via a disposable database c285_reverify created and dropped on 127.0.0.1:55432 (the shared invdev database was not used)
reverification.attributionRule: A test counts for a card when it imports one of that card's DISTINCTIVE owned modules (an owned module that is not shared API infrastructure, counting a bare import of a tool's basename because tools are imported after a sys.path insert), or when the card's own manifest checks name that test file. A first attempt matched module basenames as substrings and pulled in 128-153 files per card, which is the failure whyCiVerified names: it would have read as coverage while asserting nothing. Recorded so the next reader can judge the rule, not just the result.
